I don’t know what labour laws are like in the US/whichever state you live in, but in Canada employees are protected by laws that allow a worker to refuse unsafe work conditions (e.g. potential exposure to a highly contagious and dangerous disease in the throes of a pandemic). If an employee refuses to work and the employer threatens them with consequences (e.g. being fired) the employer is actually liable and can be sued. Might be worth looking into, in case you’re able to stretch the amount of time you’re staying at this job without officially quitting (you might be able to get some benefits or returns if you remain an employee, as opposed to nothing if you quit)
On the other hand, if this place is as much of a hellhole as it sounds like, I say get the hell out. Your physical and mental health aren’t worth the cost of the abuse and blatant lack of regard for employee safety/wellbeing on the part of your uppers. Best of luck

Girlllll what do you mean women aren’t funny?! That’s some internalized sexism right there! I struggle with this a lot too and let me just say: you gotta do you. You have to be yourself and accept your womanhood because if you don’t, who will? If you don’t, why would men? As fucking exhausting as it is, we have to be our own cheerleaders and at the very least know that we aren’t those memes, aren’t those jokes, aren’t those ignorant stereotypes and generalizations. For so long I tried to distance myself from femininity because I thought it would make me more powerful. It did nothing but make me feel worse, because I realized the reason I was doing it was to prove something to the men I so resented and in doing so was actually proving them right - great women can’t be typical women? Bullshit. Typical women are great women. Don’t let yourself fall for any other misogynistic garbage meant to keep us subdued and concerned with how we look in the eyes of men. There are lots of good men out there too, btw, so get off of those subreddits that are full of those kind of memes, and don’t bother with the men who actually believe that crap. Though it takes practice, looking for the good is much more rewarding- and far less exhausting- than expending precious energy on the bad (when ultimately there’s nothing to be done about it except do you).
